correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation of the frozen vector field gives \(\dot J=-2\beta J\) for \(J=\operatorname{Im}(\overline{x}y)\). Backward exponential growth excludes nonzero \(J\) on a bounded complete orbit. The zero-defect condition plus uniqueness fixes a common phase, and a bounded complete orbit cannot pass through \(x=y=0\). On a compact invariant support the symmetry solution \((u,v)=(X,Y)\) of the normal block is continuous, nonvanishing and therefore bounded above and away from zero, giving exponent zero; the normal trace is \(-2\beta\), so Liouville gives the second exponent \(-2\beta\).
risks: The Lyapunov splitting is only asserted on compactly supported ergodic invariant measures; no finite-time locking is asserted for generic forward transients.
